error.signature: Stripe webhook event received multiple times despite 200 response
error.regex: (duplicate.*webhook|webhook.*delivered.*twice|idempotency.*key.*conflict|Stripe\ webhook\ event\ received\ multiple\ times\ despite\ 200\ res)

verdict.summary: Stripe retries webhook delivery (with exponential backoff, for up to three days in live mode) whenever your endpoint doesn't quickly return a 2xx response, including timeouts and slow responses caused by complex processing before the response is sent - this produces duplicate deliveries of the same event ID even though the event was ultimately handled. Stripe's docs no longer publish an exact timeout threshold in seconds; the documented guidance is to return 2xx immediately and defer processing, not to rely on a specific cutoff.

dead_ends.action: Return 200 only after processing the event fully, assuming there's no meaningful risk as long as processing 'isn't too slow'
dead_ends.why_fails: Stripe's webhook docs instruct endpoints to quickly return a successful 2xx status code before any complex logic that could cause a timeout, and state that if delivery fails (including a timeout), Stripe retries with exponential backoff for up to three days in live mode - so slow processing before the response is sent produces duplicate deliveries of the same event ID.

Stripe's webhook docs describe delivery as at-least-once: 'Webhook endpoints might occasionally receive the same event more than once,' and recommend guarding against duplicates by tracking event IDs rather than assuming single delivery.

workarounds.action: Return 200 immediately, then process asynchronously via queue
workarounds.how: Receive webhook -> store raw event in DB/queue -> return 200 -> process from queue

workarounds.action: Implement idempotency using event.id as dedup key
Use Stripe's event retrieval API to verify event authenticity instead of trusting payload
workarounds.how: event = stripe.Event.retrieve(event_id) # re-fetch from Stripe API
